decisions.id: T346: a tree nobody held at the start is no task's carry

decisions.why: Keeps the existing rule for an unheld tree. The section's 27-carry pass over the pinned window found one carry re-booked and none lost, so nothing the breakdown counted is dropped.

decisions.id: T346: the carry's time stays its run's end
decisions.summary: only the holder changes; batches still compares the run's end with the landing's
decisions.why: Changes nothing the task line asks to change.

decisions.summary: make task-progress reads the same function, so its staged list and carried lines name the start holder
decisions.why: Serves the GM's live view (2026-11-26, T293). The section measured a one-line diff in the old and new outputs, the expected one.

decisions.id: T382: own lines outside every span open a span
decisions.summary: an agent's own line outside its spans opens a span to its next stop, else to span_end's end
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome: 557.5 builder-minutes over 2026-11-21 to 11-24 were left out of the builder column while their turns were booked. The GM asked for everything measured (2026-11-22) and every minute named (amendment (c)). The section measured that no new span crosses a stopped stretch.

decisions.id: T382: span starts at the first own line, not the stop
decisions.summary: the stop to the next own line stays T345's 'builders: stopped' time
decisions.why: Avoids counting the same minutes twice, which would itself distort the breakdown.

decisions.summary: a single own line with no later line or stop opens no span; an agent with no start line takes its kind from its first stop that names one, else ?
decisions.why: A lone line has no duration to book. Taking the kind from a stop keeps review agents out of the builder column, as the GM's split of reviewing from code work asks (2026-11-25). This is detail inside the requested fix and narrows nothing.

decisions.id: T382: new spans are in flight for waits
decisions.summary: Flight::book treats a new span like a started one, so blocking rises 3539.9 to 3550.8 in the 2026-11-22 window
decisions.why: Under the GM's definition (l), a wait booked to a builder that was working is a wait on that builder. A session waiting on a builder inside a span that the lines show it working is blocking on that work.

decisions.id: T346, T382: two pinned tests restated
decisions.summary: a_resumed_builder_is_booked_in_every_span_and_stopped_between_them and the_columns_book_make_runs_compile_and_until restated to the new readings
decisions.why: The tests pinned the wrong readings. Under fix-as-we-go (GM 2026-11-18), checks change as the defect they pinned is fixed. New red-first tests carry each rule.

decisions.summary: counted as performance work for scheduling
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-20: 'this kind of measurement task to be counted as a performance task for the purpose of scheduling and coming first'.

decisions.id: T346 (found and left): a bundle's carry is no task's, filed as T393
decisions.summary: tiers::batches splits a bundle's pool detail '451 T324,T345' on whitespace only, so a bundle's carry is booked to no task; not fixed here, filed T393, lands before T380
decisions.why: This is a real defect left. It is a different one from either task line: how a bundle's pool detail is parsed, not when the holder is read. Fixing it needs a new rule for which bundled task a carry run books to. The GM's own words cover filing it: 2026-11-22, 'not bother cutting back on new tasks filed ... we can file new tasks just as fast as we are now if we bundle them together when fixing them'. It is filed and ordered, not dropped. The purpose test holds: T346's own measured mis-booking (T301/T308) and every other non-bundle carry are fixed by this section, so the deferral does not gut what T346 asked. T332 and T344 are pre-existing open tasks the section reports, not decisions it makes.

decisions.summary: The memory of a one-crate test build measured before the lane was built (0.19-0.64 GiB after a body edit, at most 1.42 GiB where the crate recompiles whole), against the wide builds the slot is for.
decisions.why: T347's line asks exactly this order: measure the memory of a one-crate test build first.

decisions.summary: A lane of its own kind, one wide, knob L7R_BUILD_SLOTS_SMALL (GUESS), rather than no slot; its width argued from the 7 GiB margin's 1.6 GiB of room.
decisions.why: The line offers 'no slot or a slot of its own kind'; choosing the second, with the budget arithmetic shown and a knob, is a choice inside the offer and keeps T284's memory purpose.

decisions.summary: A build is told alone by a kept content key of everything but the crate's own sources AND every keyed file being older than the key file.
decisions.why: How the class is recognized; the file-times half is measured (git checkout recompiled a dependency at an unchanged key). Mechanism, not scope.

decisions.summary: Times read conservatively: a tie counts as newer, an unaskable time is not alone, anything unknown takes a wide slot.
decisions.why: Errs toward the behavior before the lane, which keeps T284's memory purpose; not a narrowing of the class, which is defined by what can be shown to compile one crate alone.

decisions.summary: One telling per crate per run, shared by the binary-key build and a red build's second asking; runs that ask no binary key are wide.
decisions.why: Consistency of one answer within a run; the excluded runs (FRESH=1, outside a repository, test-no-counters) are not one-crate incremental builds.

decisions.summary: The build after a healed link takes a wide slot; only the first build runs in the lane it was told.
decisions.why: After the heal drops fingerprints and incremental sessions the build is no longer of the class the lane is for; sending it wide is applying the rule, not excepting from it.

decisions.summary: No lane where L7R_BUILD_SLOTS=0 or under a holder; with the lane at 0 nothing is told and the build is wide as before.
decisions.why: Preserves the existing off switch the measuring scripts rely on and gives the new knob an off position; neither narrows the lane where slots exist.

decisions.summary: A lane that cannot be taken (no flock, the shared 900 s ceiling passed) runs the build without one and writes slot-small code 1; it never falls back to a wide slot.
decisions.why: Mirrors T284's own convention for the wide slot; refusing the wide fallback is what keeps the wait the task removes from returning.

decisions.summary: Event lines slot-tell and slot-small; a lane wait written as slot-wait so where_time books it as waiting on a build slot; measure crate unchanged.
decisions.why: Serves the line's ask to say the waiting-on-a-build-slot minutes before and after, by keeping lane waits in that same category.

decisions.summary: Module at rustc/kept/alone.rs (reads kept.rs privates), knob named L7R_BUILD_SLOTS_SMALL per the coordinating brief, the key also holds dependencies' compiled-in files and binary_args whole, the key file named by the crate's full path from the root.
decisions.why: Departures from a builder's handoff, not from the request or spec; placement and naming, or a key that is more complete (an edited include_str! target recompiles its crate), which keeps the telling correct.

decisions.summary: A build told alone never touches its key, pass or fail; a wide build writes <key>.new, renames it on a pass, removes it on a failure.
decisions.why: A behavior choice inside the lane's design: a red build of the crate alone moved no dependency, so its key still stands; removing it would send every run after a red build back to a wide slot, the wait the line asks removed. It narrows nothing asked and the key file is in the build's own target directory (no new disk residue outside it, T245/T246).

decisions.summary: A compiled-in path stops at a line's end (kept.rs INCLUDE); the defect made the first two runs after each tool rebuild tell wide.
decisions.why: A wrong outcome (a kept key differing from the same key read fresh) found in the step and fixed in it, as FIX AS WE GO requires.

decisions.summary: First build in a target directory, after a dependency edit or checkout, FRESH=1, test-no-counters, pre-warm builds, lint, cargo test --doc, make test-times, a heal's second build stay on wide slots.
decisions.why: Each is outside the class the line names (a one-crate incremental test build, whose memory was what was measured) or cannot be told to be in it; kept as before the lane, not excluded from a rule that covered them. The pre-warm's first-build gap is ruled separately as T367.

decisions.summary: make task-time's waiting-on-a-build-slot minutes AFTER the change are not given; the mechanism's wait (60 s to 1-2 ms with both wide slots held) stands in, and the day's figure is the coordinating session's to read after 24 h live, into dev/audits/build-slot.md.
decisions.why: Physically impossible inside the task: a day of builders' slot waits under the lane exists only after the lane has landed. The before figure is given, the same command is named for the after, and the controlled before/after on the mechanism carries the line's purpose (showing the wait removed) in the meantime.

decisions.summary: Two runs of one tree take turns on the run lock even with two target directories; not filed.
decisions.why: T23's existing rule, no wrong outcome; the lane is for builds of two trees, so nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Two compiling small builds of two trees queued on the lane, and the lane beside two compiling wide holders, not measured; the memory falsifier is the sampler's report.
decisions.why: The line asks for the one-crate build's memory measured first, which was; the combined figure follows from measured parts and the audit names a falsifier. No requested measurement is dropped.

decisions.summary: The pre-warm keeps no key, so a builder's first test build of each crate after a handout, sync or dependency edit is told wide though it may compile one crate alone; filed T367 (a performance task), lands before T302.
decisions.why: It narrows the lane's reach inside the class T347's line names. It is not a defect under the standing definition (no wrong outcome: the build waits as it did before the lane, nothing refuses or answers wrongly), and of what a plan leaves unfixed only a defect is NOT LEGITIMATE; it is left by the conservative telling of D3 (no key, no proof), not carved out by choice, and it is carried by a filed performance task that lands before the next step, with its size (first builds a day) to be measured first as the line's own order asks. The coordinating brief's bar on prewarm.rs is context, not the ground.

decisions.summary: A builder's lint (clippy) takes a wide slot whatever it compiles; filed T355, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Lint is not a test build, the class the line names, and its memory was not measured; the line's measure-first order keeps it wide.

decisions.summary: The coverage pass of rust/gate/crates/measure red on five lines in a pool tree where the landing's was green; filed T356, lands before T302.
decisions.why: A defect (a check refusing good work in one tree), but another crate's, found in passing and outside what T347 asks; FR-009's why, filed id and order are all stated, and it lands before T302, so it is not carried into the next step.

decisions.summary: An l7r_shared test process alive 66 minutes after its run; filed T357, lands before T302.
decisions.why: Another crate's test, found in passing, outside T347; why, id and order stated, lands before the next step.

decisions.summary: A string naming include_str! on one line is read as a compiled-in path with an empty id; filed T368, lands before T302.
decisions.why: No wrong outcome today (an empty id never moves the key); the residue of the in-task include fix, needing a token-level reader; why, id and order stated.

decisions.summary: A build-half test that asserted which wide slot each of two holders took now compares the two holders' names in either order.
decisions.why: It still requires both named holders, one in each slot, so it still pins two distinct slots taken; only the assignment order, which a just-released slot makes racy, is dropped.

decisions.summary: No test of the new module split: slowest 0.57 s, none near a second; all over a 'tenth of a second' attributed to FR-008.
decisions.why: Inside the crate's existing practice. The citation is wrong: this feature's FR-008 is the background-run and poll-interval guard and says nothing of a tenth of a second; the plan should name the rule it means. A citation error, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: The cap's exit also takes any .md file under l7r-handoffs/ that the builder's own brief names; the refusal names the brief's first such file; the <agent_id>.md rule is kept for a brief naming none.
decisions.why: FR-006 lets a builder past the threshold write 'its handoff file, naming the file'. An exit that refuses the file its brief named is a tool refusing valid input, a defect against FR-006; taking the briefed name and keeping the old rule beside it repairs it without widening the exit past handoff files.

decisions.summary: Match the briefed name rather than any name holding the task id.
decisions.why: A mechanism choice for the same FR-006 exit; it settles nothing the request or spec decides.

decisions.summary: A resume's refusal names a written briefed file first, then <agent>.md, then the brief's first, then the cap's own name, and its 'not written yet' line follows the file named.
decisions.why: FR-006's resume refusal names the handoff; naming the one actually written fixes a wrong message (a build half told its handoff is unwritten).

decisions.summary: open_handoffs counts a build half's <task>-build.md (and a bundle's) as finished, so it is no longer named beside foreign changes as their likely writer; open stays T<n>-<agent id>.md.
decisions.why: open_handoffs refuses nothing by itself; it names a likely writer in writer_refusal's message. Naming a builder that ended as briefed as an open writer is a wrong answer; reconciling the landing's reading with the briefed names narrows nothing the GM or the spec asked.

decisions.summary: A wrap-up band from the 300,000 cap to a 340,000 ceiling (a GUESS knob, falsifier in the audit) in which a builder may finish its stop point's steps; past the ceiling the guard is as before.
decisions.why: The GM's 2026-11-27 question challenges the abrupt cutoff because it stops builders 'even finishing their handoff', while conceding 'I understand wanting to hand off to a new builder'. A band that lets the stop point finish answers the question; a ceiling keeps the handoff he accepted and FR-006's threshold, and the 2026-11-26 words on closing builders out ('wary of needing to keep them around') support bounding it. The 340k figure is a coordinator's GUESS, not his words, and is labeled one.

decisions.summary: In the band: Read/Grep, a MODE 4 spec-fidelity dispatch, and Bash whose every simple command is allowed (cd, export, VAR=value, git status/diff, head/tail/grep, make decide/plan-delta/plan-verdict/claims-triage/claims-owed/task-add/task-withdraw/builder-checks), matched by invocation through shared::tree::commands; redirects not judged.
decisions.why: These are the stop point's mechanical steps the motivating builders were refused (heading: T315 and T325 'refused only the mechanical end of their stop points'); matching invocations not mentions follows the project's guard rule. The set is a strict loosening of the old guard.

decisions.summary: make plan-delta allowed though the task line's list omits it.
decisions.why: A widening of the coordinator's list toward the GM's purpose, not a narrowing of what he asked: it is the plan review's own command in every stop point and T325's refused step. Without it the band would refuse the case the request answers.

decisions.summary: A later plan-review round is admitted, judged as the original spec-fidelity MODE 4 call before review_round_hooks reroutes it.
decisions.why: T315's motivating case was a second round; admitting it serves the request directly.

decisions.summary: In the band: Edit/Write of any file but the handoff, any other dispatch (claims-triage/impl-drift dispatches included), any other target or program, and SendMessage; the main session's resume of a builder past the cap stays refused.
decisions.why: The GM's question asks that a builder be let finish its handoff, and concedes the handoff itself; it does not ask that a capped builder keep writing code. The motivating cases were refused only the mechanical end of their stop points, and the goal sends code still owed to a fresh builder 'as before'. A plan review that returns findings in the band ends in a handoff, which is the behavior he accepted, not a narrowing of the loosening he asked for. The claims dispatch is split off by the GM's 2026-11-25 ruling, so refusing it in the band keeps that rule. Keeping the resume refused follows his 2026-11-26 words on closing builders out and FR-006.

decisions.summary: Past the ceiling the old refusal and its render are unchanged ('byte for byte its old render').
decisions.why: This describes unchanged behavior the plan chose to keep (the request's 'hand off' past a limit), with existing message-store rows left valid; it is not a port held to exactness against a replacement, so the struck exactness standard does not apply.

decisions.summary: builder_stop_hooks, set_down_hooks::stalls and make task-progress unchanged; only the guard reads the ceiling.
decisions.why: Nothing in the request asks those readers to change; a band builder may still stop, and a stall is still marked.

decisions.summary: The band's refusal (wrap-up-refused) is recorded, red-first tested (suite 49 of 96 failing with the branch off), escapable by the existing CONTEXT_OK judged before the band, one message-checked wording naming what is still allowed and the handoff.
decisions.why: FR-012's three owed parts for a refusal of FR-006's guard: a red-first test, an escape of a reason, a message naming the compliant command; all three are present.

decisions.summary: Tagged [perf] under FR-013 (faster builders' loop), measured by wrap-up passes per builder against the re-read saved; T352 first, then the band.
decisions.why: FR-013 counts work that makes the builders' loop faster as performance work; the order is a dependency the spec leaves open.

decisions.summary: The clone's builder is recognized at dispatch by the block's STOP POINT line, not by reading 'orders an edit' from prose (the task line's wording).
decisions.why: Narrower than the task line's 'names the clone and orders an edit' (the line is the coordinating session's; request.md holds no T353 section and spec-cited.md is empty, so the task line is known only from the block's own quotation). Legitimate as the dispatch-time recognizer: a rule that read an edit order from prose would refuse readers, a check that refuses good work, which constitution XIV counts as a defect and which teaches bypass, so the literal reading defeats the enforcement the GM asked for (2026-11-19: 'real enforcement and not just instructions'; T285: tooling 'without the opportunity for this kind of mistake'). The bundle records the STOP line on 0 of the week's 107 non-writing dispatches. This ruling covers the recognizer only; what it leaves uncaught is ruled under T353-D1b.

decisions.summary: The residual: a hand brief with no STOP POINT line and no pool tree still passes into the session clone, and the Found-and-left item leaves it 'not filed'.
decisions.why: This is a check that passes bad work, a defect by constitution XIV's definition, and it is the incident T334 was filed for ('broke the sizing rules ... in its own briefs with nothing refusing'). It has observed instances: the block's own measurement finds 3 builders after the line existed that wrote source without it, at least 2 of them in the clone (P15 cascade, the barracks Guesses tab), plus the whole pre-line population. The item's ground, 'Not a defect seen since the block existed', contradicts those 3. Its fallback, the five post-pool dispatches, is a window the measurement paragraph itself says does 'not show the hole unused, only unused so far'. Approach item 12 names the wrong outcome as 'went out unsized', which is a visible effect, so under the found-and-left rule (FR-009, FIX AS WE GO) the item is fixed here or deferred with 'Not fixed here: <why>. Filed as T<n>; lands before T<m>.'. A defect is never left unfiled. Leaving it relies on the session remembering to use the tooling, which is what the GM's T285 and 2026-11-19 words rule out. Remedy: fix it in this task, or file it with an id and an order. This finding does not require a prose rule; T353-D1a stands. The figures should also be corrected: 357 wrote source and 23 were caught, so 334 = 357 - 23 is every uncaught writer, not 334 'all before the line' plus 3 after. By the block's own numbers 331 were before the line, and one of the 3 (T250 batch 3) was in a hand worktree, not the clone. D1's '23 of 23 builders' sits beside 26 post-line builders.

decisions.summary: The rule does not require the prompt to name the clone; the STOP line with no marker and no pool tree is enough.
decisions.why: This widens the hold rather than narrowing it: a brief naming no tree works in the session clone, so it is the same case the line asks to hold. Readers are unaffected, since they carry no STOP line.

decisions.summary: The pool-tree no-marker rule and a borne-out marker are decided first.
decisions.why: An ordering between T334's rules and the new one. Every builder the line names is still held by one rule or the other.

decisions.summary: T250 batches 5, 7 and 8 and agenda items 6 and 12, named on the task line as clone editors, are restated as hand-worktree writers and handed to T285's hand-worktree guard.
decisions.why: This corrects a factual premise of the task line from the transcripts, as constitution XIV has a claim the record does not bear out restated. The cases are not dropped: they are placed with the guard the GM asked for in T285 ('tooling ... without the opportunity for this kind of mistake'). Not verifiable from this bundle: whether T285's guard does close a hand `git worktree add` (spec-cited.md is empty). That is worth confirming, but it is not a narrowing of this block.

decisions.why: A cost measure keyed on exactly the triggers the rules act on, so no case the rules hold is skipped.

decisions.summary: The STOP line's test moves to one shared reader, `l7r_shared::builder_brief::stop_point`, which `split::is_code` now calls.
decisions.why: Implementation structure, with one reader of one convention. Nothing the GM asked for changes.

decisions.summary: The brief rule runs after the Workflow model rule, on what that rule passes; it adds refusals and never lifts one.
decisions.why: The model rule (T216/T217) is unchanged, and the requested hold is added to it.

decisions.summary: Only a literal prompt (string literals, or literals joined by +) is read; a variable or computed prompt, and `${...}` interpolations, pass unseen.
decisions.why: The ground is impossibility. The block's premise is that a Workflow's agent() call meets no Agent hook, so the script's text is the only interception point, and a static hook cannot know a runtime-built string without evaluating the script. The gap is stated in the guard's header and asserted in a test. Its reach is unmeasured, which the block says plainly, since no builder has yet been sent from a workflow. So it is a hypothetical limit, not a known defect, and 'Found and left? none' is consistent with it, unlike T353's residual, which has observed instances.

decisions.summary: The pool registry is read from the session's mirror (`session.main()`), not from the Workflow's own tree.
decisions.why: This matches how builder-brief-hooks reads the pool, so a workflow run from a pool tree sees every clone's registry. It reaches more cases, not fewer.

decisions.summary: A defined agent type stays the GUARDED rule's, check-wave units are left to the Agent hooks they already meet, and the run is refused on the first refusal with an escape logged under builder-brief.
decisions.why: FR-006 defines a builder as 'not a defined review agent', so defined types are outside the brief rule by the spec's own wording. Check-wave units are said already to meet this guard. Refusing the whole run and logging the escape follow T334-D5 and the existing workflow guard's form.
